title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A

kpis.sub: BELOW POST-IPO HIGH · STARSHIP FLIGHT 14 NOW NET SEPT 28
kpis.label: SPCX traded around $152.71 on Sept 20 — up slightly from $151.21 a week earlier and well above the $135 IPO price, but still ~32% below its $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14 (first true orbital attempt, 26 Starlink V3 satellites in Group 31-1, booster offshore landing) has slipped again, from the Sept 18/19 window to NET Sept 28

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD STARTUP FUNDING · U.S. CAPTURES ~63% OF GLOBAL TOTAL
kpis.label: Crunchbase-tracked global private investment in space/satellite startups holds at a record $20.3B for 2026, already the highest annual tally on record with roughly three months still to go; U.S. companies captured roughly $12.7B (~63%) of that total, with China at just over 20% and Europe around 10%

kpis.sub: IRIDIUM DEAL NOW FULLY FINANCED · NEUTRON STILL POINTED AT 2027
kpis.label: Rocket Lab fully funded its Iridium acquisition on Sept 15 — completing a $1.94B ATM offering and canceling the $3.6B senior secured bridge facility — and Craig-Hallum initiated coverage at Buy on Sept 18; shares remain well off their 2026 highs even as Electron flew its 96th mission (17th of 2026) on Sept 19, and Neutron's maiden flight still looks pointed at 2027

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+92% YoY), with Starlink/connectivity revenue up 66% YoY to $4.3B (~$17B annualized) and 12M subscribers, adding 500k+ new subs a month; connectivity remains the only profitable segment ($1.66B operating profit). Shares traded around $152.71 on Sept 20, up slightly from the prior week and well above the $135 IPO price, though still ~32% below the $225.64 post-IPO high
rows.watch for: Starship Flight 14 — first true orbital attempt, 26 Starlink V3 satellites (Group 31-1), booster offshore landing — has slipped again, from the Sept 18/19 window to NET Sept 28; four more share-unlock tranches through Dec 8, 2026; Starlink ARPU down 22% YoY as international/lower-priced plans scale

rows.angle: Fully funded its Iridium acquisition on Sept 15 — completing a $1.94B ATM offering and canceling the $3.6B senior secured bridge facility — and launched its 96th Electron mission overall (17th of 2026) on Sept 19; Craig-Hallum initiated coverage at Buy on Sept 18, and the company released its IMM Apex germanium-free solar cell into production on Sept 8
rows.watch for: Despite the financing milestone and fresh coverage, shares remain well off their 2026 highs; Neutron's maiden flight still looks pointed at 2027 after January's tank-pressure-test rupture, and the Iridium deal's exchange-ratio collar and mid-2027 targeted close are unchanged

rows.angle: Guggenheim initiated coverage Sept 15 at Buy with a 49% upside target, and CFO Ken Sharp presented the missiles/space/comms strategy at Morgan Stanley's Laguna Conference on Sept 16; Space and Mission Systems is tracking toward $13B+ in 2026 revenue, on top of the $4.7B Lockheed PAC-3 MSE contract and the $1.75B AMDT3 Tranche 3 award (with Sierra Space)
rows.watch for: Shares are still hovering near 52-week lows around $250-253, down more than 30% over six months, with the securities-claims investigation tied to Kubasik's August ouster still open; the new bullish coverage hasn't yet moved the stock. Also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: BlueBirds 12 and 13 are fully deployed, US Mobile is lining up a Q4 direct-to-cell launch on the network, and a new Vodafone Ukraine gateway joint venture adds to integration progress with Vodafone, Orange, Telefónica and Deutsche Telekom
rows.watch for: Shares fell about 10% even on the deployment/carrier news — a sell-the-news reaction — and the stock still carries a pending class-action lawsuit; Q2's loss came in wider than expected at $0.77/share against a reaffirmed $150-200M FY26 revenue guide

rows.angle: Completed the SXM-11 satellite handover to its customer on Sept 15 and booked a new two-unit IM 300 platform order from an undisclosed customer, on top of a record $1.8B backlog and Q2 revenue up roughly 300% YoY
rows.watch for: Shares stayed volatile — up 6.6% on Sept 17, down 5.9% the next day, settling near $13.94 — and net insider selling has reached $259.4M over the past 12 months, including director Kamal Ghaffarian's $1.48M sale right after the IM 300 order announcement

rows.angle: Q2 revenue of $116.1M (+58% YoY) delivered Planet's first profitable quarter as a public company, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.02 beating estimates
rows.watch for: Shares are down 67% from their May peak on concerns about a proposed $1.5B equity dilution plan, and CEO Will Marshall sold $2.2M of stock on Sept 15 (a scheduled tax-withholding sale tied to RSU vesting, not open-market conviction selling); shares near $16.49, testing multi-month lows

rows.angle: Record Q2 revenue of $117.1M (+89.6% YoY), record 27.8% gross margin, and a record $542.1M backlog (book-to-bill 1.42); showcased its Penguin UAS and Octopus payloads at the Sept 10-11 Rīga Conference as the largest UAS supplier in the Baltics
rows.watch for: Shares fell 7% on Sept 18 to ~$10.74 even after BofA raised its target from $7 to $8 while keeping an Underperform rating; a fresh disclosure shows $1.15B of net insider selling over the past 12 months, a scale that's hard to square with the steady-execution story and now the key watch item

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: NASA's Jared Isaacman said New Glenn Mk1 remains 'Plan A' to fly again this year and praised Blue Origin's progress since the May 28 pad explosion, but SpaceX veterans told press they still don't expect New Glenn to fly from the rebuilt pad before year-end given the scope of the infrastructure work.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Onboarded to a $981M U.S. Space Force IDIQ contract and won a NASA Spacecraft Processing Operations Contract; Roth MKM reaffirmed Buy on Sept 13 while Morgan Stanley kept Hold. Shares trade around $20-21, down about 53% over the past 12 months, with a SpaceX rideshare crunch still seen as a tailwind for Firefly's and Rocket Lab's dedicated small-launch businesses.

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Unveiled Nova Block 2 on Sept 8 — a larger 5-meter fairing and non-tapered second stage capable of 15 metric tons to LEO fully reusable (23 tons expendable) — alongside the $1B Series E close (total raised $2.3B, ~$10B valuation); the original Nova Pathfinder's first flight has already slipped from 'end of 2026' to 'early 2027,' with Block 2 now targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Rocket Lab's Iridium financing alone required a $1.94B dilutive ATM offering on top of the earlier bridge facility, and Stoke Space's $1B Series E (total raised $2.3B) is funding a Nova Block 2 that isn't now targeted until 2029; ASTS's $1B convertible notes remain a separate overhang.

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue still runs through NASA/DoD — L3Harris just landed a new $4.7B Lockheed PAC-3 MSE contract and Guggenheim initiated it at Buy, yet shares remain stuck near 52-week lows with a securities-claims investigation unresolved; the Pentagon's SHIELD IDIQ vehicle has ballooned to 2,400+ qualified vendors, diluting any one company's edge in winning Golden Dome work.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX sits ~32% below its post-IPO high and even its own marquee catalyst keeps slipping: Starship Flight 14 has now moved from Sept 15 to Sept 18/19 to NET Sept 28. Meanwhile RDW's record Q2 didn't stop a fresh $1.15B insider-selling disclosure and a 7% one-day drop, another sign of the gap between operating results and price across the sector.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or slipped date can move a small-cap sharply: Starship Flight 14 has slipped three times in three weeks, Stoke's Nova Pathfinder is already pushed to early 2027, Neutron still looks pointed at 2027 after January's tank-pressure-test rupture, and Blue Origin's New Glenn return-to-flight target faces open skepticism from SpaceX veterans. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab launches 96th Electron mission
catalysts.description: Rocket Lab completed its 96th Electron launch overall, the 17th of 2026, from New Zealand, extending its record cadence for the year.

catalysts.title: Redwire slides on insider-selling disclosure despite BofA target hike
catalysts.description: BofA raised its Redwire price target from $7 to $8 while keeping an Underperform rating; shares still fell 7% to ~$10.74 as a fresh disclosure showed $1.15B of net insider selling over the trailing 12 months. Separately, Craig-Hallum initiated Rocket Lab at Buy.

catalysts.title: L3Harris presents at Morgan Stanley's Laguna Conference
catalysts.description: CFO Ken Sharp reiterated the multi-domain sensing, spectrum dominance and missiles strategy, a day after Guggenheim initiated coverage at Buy with a 49% upside target.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab fully funds Iridium acquisition; Intuitive Machines completes SXM-11 handover
catalysts.description: Rocket Lab completed a $1.94B ATM offering and canceled its $3.6B Iridium bridge facility; the same day, Intuitive Machines handed over the SXM-11 satellite to its customer and Planet Labs' CEO sold $2.2M of stock in a scheduled tax-withholding transaction.

catalysts.title: AST SpaceMobile deployment and carrier news meets a sell-the-news drop
catalysts.description: BlueBirds 12 and 13 fully deployed and a new Vodafone Ukraine gateway JV and US Mobile Q4 direct-to-cell launch plan were announced, but ASTS shares fell about 10% on the news.

catalysts.title: Starship Flight 14 slips again, now NET Sept 28
catalysts.description: An updated FCC filing pushed SpaceX's first true Starship orbital attempt — carrying 26 Starlink V3 satellites — from the Sept 18/19 window to no earlier than Sept 28.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, VSAT, MDA, ASTS top holdings); roughly +45-50% YTD — PL's 67%-from-peak collapse and RDW's insider-selling headline have pulled the index down from earlier-summer highs, partially offset by RKLB's Iridium-financing news

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed, broader tech adjacency; roughly +20-24% YTD — continues to lag the pure-play index funds as its broader tech-adjacent holdings dilute pure space-sector momentum

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight, space + defense + deep-sea blend; roughly +50-55% YTD — L3Harris's persistence near 52-week lows remains a drag on the defense side even as new analyst coverage argues the stock is undervalued

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Fully funded its Iridium acquisition on Sept 15 — completing a $1.94B ATM offering and canceling the $3.6B bridge facility — resolving the financing-risk bear case while Craig-Hallum initiated at Buy and Electron flew its 96th mission (17th of 2026) on Sept 19; raising weight as the deal de-risks even though Neutron still isn't flying before 2027.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Guggenheim initiated coverage Sept 15 at Buy with 49% upside and Space & Mission Systems revenue is tracking to top $13B in 2026, but shares are still hovering near 52-week lows around $250 with the Kubasik-era securities investigation unresolved; raising weight modestly as new analyst conviction argues the backlog isn't being credited. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: Shares fell 7% on Sept 18 even as BofA raised its target to $8 (still Underperform), and a fresh disclosure shows $1.15B of net insider selling over the past 12 months — a scale that dwarfs the roughly $1B market cap and is hard to square with the 'consistent execution' thesis; cutting weight sharply pending clarity on what's driving that selling.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: BlueBird 12/13 are fully deployed and US Mobile is lining up a Q4 direct-to-cell launch alongside a new Vodafone Ukraine gateway JV, yet shares fell 10% on the news — a sell-the-news reaction that looks more like market noise than a thesis break; nudging weight up as commercial integration keeps advancing.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: Completed the SXM-11 satellite handover Sept 15 and carries a record $1.8B backlog, but shares stayed volatile (+6.6% then -5.9% in consecutive sessions) and insider selling remains heavy ($259.4M net over 12 months); raising size modestly but keeping it small given that selling pattern.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Shares sit around $152.71, still ~32% below the $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14 — the first true orbital attempt with 26 Starlink V3 satellites — has slipped again, now NET Sept 28. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Shares are down 67% from their May peak on a proposed $1.5B equity dilution plan, and the CEO sold $2.2M of stock Sept 15 (scheduled tax-withholding, not open-market conviction selling, but it adds to the overhang); staying on Watch until the dilution terms and next guide are clearer.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Rocket Lab fully financed the acquisition on Sept 15 — canceling the bridge facility and targeting a mid-2027 close — which lowers deal-completion risk, but the exchange-ratio economics are unchanged and RKLB stock remains the cleaner way to express the same view.
